units.title: Introduction to Biology
points: Define biology and list its main branches
State characteristics of living organisms
Compare plants and animals
Explain the importance of biology

units.title: Classification
points: Name the five kingdoms and give examples
State the major taxonomic units and their order
Apply binomial nomenclature rules
Construct and use dichotomous keys
Identify features of Arthropoda and Chordata classes

units.title: Classification II
points: State general principles of classification
State general characteristics of the five kingdoms
Outline main characteristics of major divisions of Plantae and of Arthropoda and Chordata…
Describe classes of spermatophyta
Construct and use simple dichotomous keys

units.title: The Cell
points: Identify parts of the light microscope and their functions
Calculate magnification and estimate cell size
Relate cell organelles to their functions
Compare plant and animal cells
Describe cell specialisation, tissues and organs

units.title: Cell specialization, tissues, organs
points: Describe cell specialization
State the differences between cells, tissues, organs and organ systems
Give examples of tissues, organs and organ systems

units.title: Cell Physiology
points: Explain diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Describe water relations in plant cells
Predict results of experiments on osmosis
Relate surface area to volume to exchange
Interpret plasmolysis and haemolysis observations

units.title: Nutrition in Plants
points: Describe the process of photosynthesis
Identify factors affecting photosynthesis
Explain the role of chlorophyll and light
Describe mineral salt uptake and deficiency symptoms
Interpret starch and light experiment results

units.title: Nutrition in Animals
points: Describe dentition of carnivore, herbivore and omnivore
Explain digestion in the human alimentary canal
State roles of enzymes and digestive secretions
Explain the role of vitamins and mineral salts
Outline causes and treatment of dental diseases

units.title: Transport in Plants and Animals
points: Explain absorption of water and mineral salts by roots
Describe transpiration and factors affecting it
Relate leaf and stem structure to transport
Describe blood circulation and the mammalian heart
Explain blood groups and immunity basics

units.title: Gaseous Exchange and Respiration
points: Describe gaseous exchange in plants
Compare gaseous exchange in mammals and fish
Explain aerobic and anaerobic respiration
Interpret breathing rate and experiment data
State adaptations of respiratory surfaces

units.title: Excretion and Homeostasis
points: Describe structure and function of the kidney and nephron
Explain osmoregulation and urine formation
Describe skin structure and temperature regulation
Outline excretion in plants
Interpret kidney failure and dialysis questions

units.title: Excretion and homeostasis in plants
points: Outline excretion and homeostasis in unicellular organisms
Describe excretion and homeostasis in plants
Describe excretion in mammals
Relate kidney and skin structure to their functions

units.title: Reproduction
points: Describe flower structure and parts of the seed
Explain pollination, fertilisation and fruit formation
Compare reproduction in mammals and plants
Describe the menstrual cycle and hormones
Outline asexual reproduction methods in plants

units.title: Genetics and Variation
points: Define terms: gene, allele, genotype, phenotype
Use monohybrid crosses and Punnett squares
Explain sex determination and inheritance of traits
Distinguish continuous from discontinuous variation
Discuss causes and importance of variation

units.title: Evolution and Ecology
points: Outline evidence for evolution
Explain natural selection and adaptation
Describe food chains, webs and trophic levels
Explain energy flow and nutrient cycles
Describe factors affecting populations in habitats

syllabus.name: Edexcel A Level Economics A (9EC0), Paper 2

units.title: Measures of economic performance
points: Calculate and interpret GDP, real GDP and GDP per capita
Distinguish GDP from GNI and explain the limitations of GDP
Measure inflation with CPI and RPI and explain their uses
Distinguish unemployment measures: claimant count vs ILO/LFS
Interpret the current account of the balance of payments
Explain index numbers and use them in data interpretation

units.title: Aggregate demand
points: Define AD and explain its components (C + I + G + X − M)
Explain the downward slope of the AD curve
Analyse the determinants of consumption and the APC/APS
Explain investment and the accelerator effect
Distinguish injections and withdrawals
Show shifts in AD on a diagram and analyse their effects

units.title: Aggregate supply
points: Explain the shape of the short-run AS curve
Show the effect of a change in costs on short-run AS
Distinguish short-run from long-run AS
Illustrate the Keynesian long-run AS curve and its stages
Explain factors shifting long-run AS (quantity and quality of inputs)
Use AD/AS diagrams to show macroeconomic equilibrium

units.title: National income
points: Explain the circular flow of income
Distinguish equilibrium and full-employment level of output
Show equilibrium with injections and withdrawals
Calculate and explain the multiplier
Use the multiplier formula and apply it to a change in injections
Explain the significance of the multiplier for policy

units.title: Economic growth
points: Distinguish actual and potential growth and their causes
Show growth on a PPF and AD/AS diagram
Explain output gaps: positive and negative
Describe the trade (business) cycle and its phases
Explain benefits and costs of economic growth
Evaluate whether growth is always desirable

units.title: Macroeconomic objectives and policy
points: Explain objectives: growth, inflation target, employment, BoP, redistribution
Explain demand-side policies: fiscal and monetary
Analyse fiscal policy and automatic stabilisers
Explain monetary policy tools and transmission mechanism
Explain supply-side policies: market-based and interventionist
Evaluate conflicts and trade-offs between objectives and policies

units.title: Globalisation, trade and trading blocs
points: Explain causes and consequences of globalisation
Explain specialisation, comparative and absolute advantage
Analyse patterns and changes in trade
Calculate and interpret terms of trade
Explain trading blocs and the role of the WTO
Explain methods and effects of protectionism

units.title: Balance of payments and exchange rates
points: Explain the components of the current and financial accounts
Analyse causes of current account deficits and surpluses
Explain fixed, floating and managed exchange rate systems
Analyse factors influencing exchange rates (e.g. interest rates)
Explain depreciation/appreciation and their effects on trade
Explain international competitiveness and its determinants

units.title: Poverty, inequality and development
points: Distinguish absolute and relative poverty and their causes
Explain measures of income and wealth inequality (e.g. Lorenz curve, Gini)
Evaluate measures of development (HDI, GNI per capita, MPI)
Explain factors influencing growth and development
Evaluate strategies to promote growth and development (aid, trade, FDI)
Relate development strategies to government policy choices

units.title: Financial sector and public finance
points: Explain the role of financial markets and key institutions
Explain market failure in the financial sector
Explain the role and tools of central banks, including QE
Explain the role and effects of public expenditure
Analyse taxation: types, incidence and effects
Explain public sector finances: budget deficits, debt and the fiscal rules
